newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian policeman to go on trial for massacre.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian policeman to go on trial for massacre.

text.p: The first of 52 police officers accused of arbitrarily gunning down 21 residents of a Rio shantytown in August 1993 is due to go on trial on Thursday, a court official said.
Paulo Roberto Alvarenga claims to be innocent and asked to be judged as soon as possible.
The judge in the case postponed the trial of another 16 policemen because new forensic evidence implicated officers who were initially arrested but later freed.

The policemen are accused of involvement in the slayings in the Vigario Geral slum on August 30, 1993, when 20 hooded gunmen dressed in black and armed with automatic weapons and shotguns opened fire on residents to avenge the death of four policemen.
The massacre, in which 21 people were killed and four wounded, took place hours after four military police officers were killed in an ambush by alleged drug traffickers in the shantytown.
A total of 52 policemen are being tried for the slayings in two separate court processes, including 19 officers who were denounced by their colleagues after they had been arrested.

The new evidence was obtained after bodies of 19 massacre victims were exhumed in October to be re-checked for bullet wounds. Relatives of victims had found bullets in the other two bodies that led authorities to review the original autopsies.

The accused face sentences of several hundred years in jail if found guilty on charges of murder and attempted murder. Under Brazilian law, however, no one can serve more than 30 years, regardless of sentence.
